Relabel a categorical variable by name, never by position

Source: R/categorical_guard.R
relbl.Rd

Gives a factor or character vector new labels with a mapping written by name, old label = new label, and returns a factor. Assigning a vector of labels by position (the levels(x) <- ... idiom, or factor(x, labels = ...) with labels in a different order from the codes) is how the four race categories were rotated in the analysis that the Ontario Human Rights Commission corrected on 26 January 2023; this function refuses unnamed mappings outright, and refuses levels that the mapping does not cover.

Usage

relbl(x, map, keep = character())

Arguments

x

A factor or character vector.

map

Named character vector, old label = new label. Every level of x must appear as a name unless listed in keep. Several old labels may map to one new label.

keep

Character vector, default empty: levels allowed to pass through unchanged.

Value

A factor with the new labels, levels in the order of mapping, carrying a recode_audit attribute (see grdrcd).

Details

The old levels are levels(x) for a factor and the sorted distinct values otherwise; all of them must be names of map or members of keep, so for a factor even an unused level must be mapped. The recode itself is grdrcd. The levels of the result are the distinct values of map in the order given, followed by the keep labels that occur in the data.

Errors: map without names (including a plain vector of new labels); a level with no mapping.

See also

grdrcd, rlblfrns, declbld

Examples

f <- factor(c("W", "B", "O", "W"))
relbl(f, c(W = "White", B = "Black", O = "Other"))
#> [1] White Black Other White
#> attr(,"recode_audit")
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$mapping
#>     W     B     O 
#> White Black Other 
#> 
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$kept
#> character(0)
#> 
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$checksum
#> [1] 992b6c4a35a3cea9e5875c90f562a3259fe9f08f1eb2fac9754d7c5b5f52bdd3
#> 
#> Levels: White Black Other

# the level order follows the mapping, not the alphabet
levels(relbl(f, c(W = "White", O = "Other", B = "Black")))
#> [1] "White" "Other" "Black"

# a kept label passes through
relbl(c("W", "B", "X"), c(W = "White", B = "Black"), keep = "X")
#> [1] White Black X    
#> attr(,"recode_audit")
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$mapping
#>     W     B 
#> White Black 
#> 
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$kept
#> [1] X
#> 
#> attr(,"recode_audit")$checksum
#> [1] ec818263ffb31defd682d27e1321fa8ea63f3f231b36b6b99fba61dca9510602
#> 
#> Levels: White Black X

# positional labels are refused
try(relbl(f, c("Black", "Other", "White")))
#> Error : relabel: `map` must be NAMED (old label = new label). Assigning labels by POSITION is how four race codes were rotated in a published analysis (OHRC correction, 26 January 2023): the labels were in alphabetical order, the codes were not.
